modelingNotes: Washington Square Fountain (Tisch Fountain) — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/washington-square-fountain.ts
Map frame: x east, y north, z up, metres; origin at the centre of the basin. Placed at bearing 32°, so +y points up the park's axis at the arch, which the 2009 rebuild aligned the fountain with.

The OSM water polygon (way/959929617, shared with the retaining wall way/1232773488) is a circle of radius 11.73 m, so the outer foot of the rim is exactly that. Inside: a low moulded granite rim with a broad seat, two seating steps down to a flat muted-blue pool, a stone drum at the centre carrying the tall jet, and eight square pedestals around the rim, as in the photos. Everything is a solid of revolution or repeated by rotation, so the model is exactly round and nothing passes the polygon's edge.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "washington-square-fountain", model "washington-square-fountain"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/c3921f733df14b41e1f6d15853cce7b343886f17/generators/washington-square-fountain.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
